name: F-5 Permanent Residence

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 consecutive years of legal residence in Korea on a qualifying visa (commonly D-7, E-7, or F-2).
requirements.fix_path: Continue accruing 5 consecutive years on a qualifying visa status.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires annual income of at least twice Korea's per-capita GNI -- KRW 104,832,000/year based on the Bank of Korea's 10 March 2026 GNI announcement; a working spouse's or cohabiting family member's income can be combined toward this threshold, provided the applicant's own income is more than 50% of the total (except where the applicant is raising a minor child).
requirements.fix_path: Document individual or combined household income at or above the current 2x-GNI threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires completion of KIIP (Korea Immigration & Integration Program) Level 5, or a score of 60 or higher on the comprehensive permanent-residence-and-naturalisation evaluation -- TOPIK alone is not accepted for this specific requirement, despite being commonly cited as sufficient in several outdated guides.
requirements.fix_path: Complete KIIP through Level 5, or sit the comprehensive evaluation and score 60+.

requirement_groups.name: F-5-16: fast track for F-2-7 points-visa holders

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 3 years holding F-2-7 (Points-Based Long-Term Resident) status specifically, rather than the general 5-year track.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain F-2-7 status first (see kr_f2_7_points_resident), then hold it for 3 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires annual income of at least 1x Korea's per-capita GNI -- significantly lower than the F-5-1 general track's 2x-GNI floor, a genuine, deliberate incentive built into the points-visa pathway.
requirements.fix_path: Document income at or above the current 1x-GNI threshold.

requirement_groups.name: F-5-2: spouse of a Korean national (F-6 holder)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 2+ years on F-6 (Marriage Migrant) status.
requirements.fix_path: Hold F-6 status for 2 years first (see kr_f6_marriage_migrant).

requirements.blocker_text: Requires income of at least 1x GNI, combinable with the Korean spouse's income.
requirements.fix_path: Document combined household income at or above 1x GNI.

evidence_required.document: 5 (or 3, or 2) years of continuous ARC/residence records on the applicable qualifying track
Income documentation meeting the applicable GNI multiple
KIIP Level 5 completion certificate or comprehensive-evaluation score of 60+

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (ARC-equivalent card renewed periodically as a card only)

sources.title: HiKorea -- Korea Immigration Service's official portal for visa categories, ARC, and stay procedures
Bank of Korea (bok.or.kr) -- official press release archive; 10 March 2026 release confirming 2025 per-capita GNI of KRW 52,416,000
KR Insider -- Complete Guide to F-5 Permanent Residency Status in Korea (2026), the source for the F-5-16 fast-track figures (3 years, 1x GNI)
HaniSeoul -- F-6 Marriage Visa Guide, the source for the F-5-2 spouse fast-track figures (2 years, 1x GNI)

notes: F-5 is genuinely not a single route but a family of over 25 sub-codes sharing one final status, per multiple independent sources -- this file models the three most structurally distinct and commonly-used tracks as OR-logic requirement_groups (general 5-year, F-2-7 fast-track, F-6-spouse fast-track), the same schema mechanism validated repeatedly elsewhere in this dataset (Poland's permanent-residence four-way split, UK Global Talent). Sub-codes not modeled here but confirmed to exist include F-5-24 (technology-startup track for D-8-4/OASIS holders, see kr_d8_4_oasis_startup's notes) and investment-based tracks (F-5-21, F-5-25) tied to specific government-approved investment programs (IISPB) -- flagged as candidates for future expansion of this route file rather than separate files, since they share F-5's single Outcome shape. LIVE DISCREPANCY CAUGHT: one otherwise well-sourced 2026 guide explicitly corrects itself mid-article, stating that TOPIK is 'not accepted as an F-5 language requirement, despite what many older guides still say' -- the correct standard is KIIP Level 5 or a 60+ score on the dedicated permanent-residence comprehensive evaluation. This is exactly the live-staleness pattern this dataset exists to catch, and it was caught here via the same source that corrected it rather than requiring independent verification, a useful reminder that even secondary sources sometimes self-correct in ways worth surfacing. The three qualifying groups' costs (5yr/2xGNI vs 3yr/1xGNI vs 2yr/1xGNI) form a clear, deliberate policy gradient rewarding the points-based skilled-talent and marriage-to-citizen tracks over the plain-residence track -- worth surfacing as a structural finding on any comparison view, since it shows Korea's immigration system actively steering applicants toward specific tracks rather than treating all qualifying paths as neutral alternatives.
